title: Function call parsing scratchpad - fragmented args
content:
Quick personal notes: investigating a recurring parsing error where the RT (runtime) rejects function call arguments as invalid JSON. Intermittent, more common on streaming responses and under load.

1) Symptom summary
- Client receives a model response that includes function_call metadata, e.g. "function_call": {"name": "save_contact", "arguments": "{\"name\": \"Alice\", \"email\": \"alice@example.com\"}" }
- Sometimes arguments string is truncated/has stray characters and JSON.parse fails in the router/validator. Example observed payloads below.
- Error in logs: "validate_function_args: invalid JSON for function save_contact: Unexpected end of JSON input"

2) Repro steps (what I ran locally)
- Basic curl to hosted API (no streaming):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"model":"gptx-3.5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"save contact Alice alice@example.com"}],"function_call":{"name":"save_contact","arguments_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"email":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name","email"]}}}' | jq .
- Result: works reliably when not streaming.

- Streaming test (curl + chunked):
  curl -s -N -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"stream":true,...}'
  Observed chunked events: some chunks end mid-JSON string for the function_call.arguments field.

- Python streaming (requests, iter_lines):
  r = requests.post(url, json=payload, stream=True, headers=headers)
  for line in r.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
    if line:
      try:
        obj = json.loads(line)
      except JSONDecodeError as e:
        # saw truncated argument strings here
        print('json decode failed', line[:200])

3) Representative bad outputs captured
- Case A (truncated):
  {"id":"msg-11","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","function_call":{"name":"save_contact","arguments":"{\"name\": \"Alice\", \"email\": \"alice@exampl\"}"}}],"done":true}
  -> arguments ends with "alice@exampl" and then server tries to validate -> JSON error.

- Case B (escaped double-quote leakage):
  {"choices":[{"message":{"function_call":{"name":"save_contact","arguments":"{\"name\": \"Bob\", \"notes\": \"He said \"call me\" tomorrow\"}"}}]}
  -> inner escaped quotes are double-escaped through some transport step, validator complains about unexpected backslashes.

- Case C (split across events):
  event 1: {"choices":[{"message":{"function_call":{"name":"save_contact","arguments":"{\"name\": \"Carla\", \"email\": \"carla@exam"
  event 2: ple.com\"}"}}],"done":true}
  -> If consumer treats each line as an independent JSON document, second piece alone is invalid.

4) Hypotheses (ranked)
- H1: Streaming/event framing: server splits the JSON string across SSE/chunk boundaries; some consumers attempt to parse per-line instead of reconstructing the full message. (Most likely)
- H2: Escaping mismatch: runtime serializes arguments twice (escape for wire + escape for JSON string) causing inconsistent escaping; some clients unescape differently. (possible)
- H3: Upstream model output contains unbalanced quotes/newlines that cause the server's serializer to produce broken payloads. (less likely but seen in stress tests)
- H4: A proxy/ingress (edge load balancer) is injecting newlines or truncating chunks at MAX_BUFFER settings, causing mid-string truncation. (in envs with heavy traffic)

5) Things tried so far (and results)
- Adjusted client to buffer SSE/events until "done" or full event id seen: reduced failures by ~85% in local tests.
- Switched to base64-encoding of function args inside a wrapper field (server-side dev experiment): eliminated JSON parse errors because raw bytes preserved, but client change required. Not final.
- Added a temporary post-processor to attempt to stitch adjacent lines if last char of line is not a valid JSON terminator ("}" or "]"). This reduced false negatives but is hacky and fragile.
- Forced single-line responses by disabling streaming on the API: reliable but increases latency and memory footprint. Not acceptable for low-latency use cases.
- Reproduced escaped-quote double-escape by running runtime with DEBUG_SERIALIZER=1. Confirmed that serializer sometimes escapes again when input already escaped. That points to serialization code path being invoked twice.

6) Local TODOs / next steps
- [ ] Add instrumentation to log raw bytes for a few failing requests (server side) -> get precise chunk boundaries. Coordinate with SRE to capture a 1-hour window. (ask Rajat to help)
- [ ] Add test harness emulating slow stream that yields partial JSON to ensure client libraries reconstruct properly.
- [ ] Propose a short-term mitigation: add "function_call_bytes" as an optional base64 field in the LLM response (backend feature flag) so clients can prefer raw bytes when streaming. Draft RFC.
- [ ] Patch serializer to avoid double-escaping: trace call sites and ensure arguments are only stringified once before top-level JSON encode.
- [ ] Update SDKs to provide a robust streaming consumer that reassembles messages before JSON.parse (node/python/ts clients).

7) Suggested long-term fixes (for design doc)
- Standardize streaming protocol: send a small envelope per event with sequence numbers and a final "end_of_message" marker so the client can reassemble multi-chunk logical messages.
- Define stable binary field for function_call.arguments (either base64 or a length-prefixed chunk) so that arbitrary bytes (including nested escapes) don’t break JSON parsing.
- Add server-side validation tolerance: if JSON.parse fails on arguments, attempt a safe stitch + reparse step (log at WARN once, then fail).

8) Notes for handoff to runtime team
- Repro artifacts: sample captured bad streams above, plus temp script (attached in linked PR) that simulates partial-chunk delivery.
- Likely landing zones: serialization module (serializer.go/serializer.py), streaming SSE handler (streaming_handler.py), and edge LB keepalive/buffer config.
- Priority: P1 for dedicated/enterprise customers using streaming + function_call heavily. For hosted users, flag with advisory if streaming is enabled.

9) Quick fixes I can ship in SDKs right now
- Node/py SDKs: provide a default buffer that reassembles events until the top-level message has matching braces before JSON.parse. Expose an escape hatch to disable.
- Add an SDK test that asserts function_call.arguments JSON.parse succeeds for artificially split streams.

10) Open questions
- Should we treat function_call.arguments as an opaque binary payload at transport level? Tradeoffs with human-readability and logs.
- If we implement a base64 field, how to migrate existing clients? Backward-compatible envelope required.

Notes-to-self: talk with Maya about telemetry aggregation (how many users hit this) and with SRE about LB chunking config. Keep this doc updated with raw captures. When we have deterministic reproduction, open CON ticket with minimal trace.

-- end of scratchpad --
